title: The design signature and the natural designers
statement: The corpus engages the design-inference debate on a distinctive footing: the canon's premise that terrestrial life was designed by the Elohim (woh-claim-0001) is stated directly; the corpus reports, in their own voice and with the critical replies, the scientists who have argued that life may have been deliberately seeded (Crick and Orgel's directed panspermia; Crick's Life Itself) or that its unguided origin is mathematically improbable, usually alongside panspermia (Hoyle and Wickramasinghe); and it rejects the supernatural designer of the intelligent-design movement — the canon's designers are natural, evolved elsewhere, themselves created (woh-claim-0030). Mainstream biology does not accept that design has been detected; a minority of scientists have argued for seeding or for the improbability of an unguided origin, and the corpus reports them as such.

includes: The canon's premise, stated directly: terrestrial life, humanity included, was designed and engineered by the Elohim (woh-claim-0001)

The position statement: natural, non-supernatural designers as a third option between the ID movement's designer and unguided abiogenesis — with the created-creators chain (woh-claim-0030) absorbing the regress objection Dawkins raised in the moment the article anchors on

The minority scientific literature, reported in its own voice with its replies: directed panspermia, the proposal that life may have been deliberately seeded (Crick and Orgel 1973; Crick 1981), and the improbability of an unguided terrestrial origin argued with panspermia (Hoyle and Wickramasinghe)
The engagement with Meyer at the article's hinge: what the signature argument would need to show, and where the corpus's position departs from the ID movement's

The honesty clause, which is the record's spine: mainstream biology does not accept that design has been detected in terrestrial life; a minority of scientists have argued for deliberate seeding or for the improbability of an unguided origin, and the corpus reports them as a minority position
excludes: Presenting the detection of design as established science or as mainstream consensus; the minority arguments are reported in their own voice, with the replies
Endorsement of the ID movement's arguments, institutions, or designer
The synthetic-biology analogy as proof (minimal-genome engineering shows design is possible, not that it happened)
The corpus's own probability modelling of abiogenesis; others' improbability arguments are reported, not computed

source_references.locator: The canon's laboratory-creation account, whose designers this record characterizes as natural and created
Meyer's information-argument programme — the strongest statement of the signature intuition, engaged and departed from
Icarus 19 (1973): the scientific formulability of designed terrestrial life
The synthetic-genome work as possibility demonstration (design of life is an existing engineering practice)
The book-length development of directed panspermia and of the difficulty of an unguided terrestrial origin (locator not verified)

alternatives.statement: Evolutionary biology explains the appearance of design; there is no signature to account for, and the intuition the position takes seriously is the illusion Darwin dissolved.
Natural designers who left no discriminating evidence are as untestable as supernatural ones; naturalizing the designer does not empiricize the claim.
Citing Crick-Orgel and synthetic biology borrows scientific respectability for a religious doctrine — the patronizing-parasitism critique applied to this exact move.

revision_triggers: Claim woh-claim-0001 or woh-claim-0030 is revised or retired.
A discriminating biological test between designed and evolved terrestrial life is proposed and survives review — in either direction, this record must move.
Public prose begins presenting design detection as established science or mainstream consensus, or endorsing ID-movement arguments, both of which this record excludes.
The article's Meyer engagement is revised at its hinge.
